---
title: Versions and citation
description: latest vs dated weekly vs monthly releases, how to pin a version, and how to cite bioc-on-ice.
---

bioc-on-ice publishes three kinds of versions. They hold the same tables in the
same layout. They differ in how long they last and how you use them
([ADR-0016](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-on-ice/blob/main/docs/adr/0016-release-cadence-weekly-r2-monthly-hf.md)).
[Releases](../releases.qmd) lists the ones available now.

| Version | Where | Changes? | Kept | Use it by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `latest/` | `https://data.bioconice.cancerdatasci.org/latest/` | with each weekly release | always the newest | querying in place |
| Dated | `https://data.bioconice.cancerdatasci.org/v{YYYY-MM-DD}/` | never | the 4 newest, about four weeks | querying in place |
| Monthly | Hugging Face dataset `seandavis/bioconice`, git tag `YYYY-MM` | never | permanently | downloading, then querying locally |

`latest/` and the dated folders are served for querying in place: DuckDB
`ATTACH`, `read_parquet` and the [Explorer](../explorer/index.qmd) all read
them over HTTPS. The monthly releases are the long-term archive and the version
to cite. Download one, then query it locally.

::: callout-note
`v2026-11-01` is the first official release: the first to pass the release
gate. Earlier, ungated releases were removed. It is also the first monthly
Hugging Face release (`2026-11`). Only the newest 4 dated releases are kept;
the weekly schedule
([#213](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-on-ice/issues/213)) runs from the
following Sunday.
:::

## Which one to use

- **Exploring, or building something that should track the sources:** use `latest/`.
- **An analysis you'll rerun in the next few weeks:** pin a dated folder.
- **A paper, a shared pipeline, a Bioconductor release, or anything you'll cite:** download a monthly release.

## Pin a dated folder

Replace `latest/` with a date. Each dated folder's `bioconice.duckdb` reads
its own Parquet files, so the views stay pinned too:

```{.sql .no-shell}
ATTACH 'https://data.bioconice.cancerdatasci.org/v2026-11-01/bioconice.duckdb' AS bioc (READ_ONLY);
```

To see which dates are available, open [Releases](../releases.qmd) or the
[folder listing](https://bioconice.cancerdatasci.org/data/). Older folders are
deleted, so use a monthly release for anything longer than a few weeks.

## Use a monthly release

Once a month, the first weekly release that passed the gate is copied to the
Hugging Face dataset `seandavis/bioconice` and tagged with its month (e.g.
`2026-11`). Files sit at the repository root in the same layout as R2
(`annotation/gene.parquet`, …).

Download the release with the [`hf` command-line
tool](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/guides/cli) (in
`huggingface_hub`; `uvx --from huggingface_hub hf` runs it without
installing), then query the local files:

```bash
hf download seandavis/bioconice --repo-type dataset --revision 2026-11 \
  --local-dir bioconice-2026-11
duckdb -c "SELECT count(*) FROM 'bioconice-2026-11/annotation/gene.parquet'"
```

`--include 'annotation/*'` downloads only some of the files. A [Hugging Face
token](https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens) (`hf auth login`) raises the
download rate limits.

Don't query the archive in place with `hf://` paths. Hugging Face limits
anonymous requests, one query can make hundreds, and repeated queries soon fail
with HTTP 429. For in-place queries use `latest/` or a dated folder.

## Cite bioc-on-ice

Cite the monthly release you used by its tag (e.g. `seandavis/bioconice@2026-11`),
and its DOI if the dataset page for that tag shows one.

If you used a dated folder instead, record its URL and the `release` and
`git_sha` from its `manifest.json`. The folder will be gone within weeks, so a
monthly release is the better thing to cite. Each table also names the
upstream source and version it came from; cite those sources as they ask (for
example, [BugSigDB](../sources/bugsigdb.qmd) is CC BY 4.0).

## The manifest

Every version has a `manifest.json`:

```bash
curl -s https://data.bioconice.cancerdatasci.org/latest/manifest.json
```

DuckDB reads it directly. The provenance fields of the current `latest/`:

```sql
SELECT release, published_at, git_sha
FROM read_json('https://data.bioconice.cancerdatasci.org/latest/manifest.json');
```

And the row count of each published table:

```sql
SELECT t.schema, t."table", t.row_count
FROM read_json('https://data.bioconice.cancerdatasci.org/latest/manifest.json'),
     unnest(tables) AS u(t)
ORDER BY t.schema, t."table";
```

- `release` is the release date and `git_sha` the commit of the [pipeline code](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-on-ice) that built it.
- `provenance` lists each upstream source with its version, URL, retrieval time and row count.
- `tables` gives each table's `path`, `row_count`, `bytes`, `sha256`, comment and column docs.
